I just tried it out, and you can attach a "submit" event handler to body, but only when the button is in a form:

```js
// works:
document.body.append(document.createElement('form'))
document.querySelector('form').append(document.createElement('button'), { textContent: 'click me' }))
document.body.addEventListener('submit', console.log)

// does not work
document.body.append(document.createElement('button'), { textContent: 'click me' }))
document.body.addEventListener('submit', console.log)
```

This means we can change the setup to always put the CR in a form, and in the test attach a listener to body's submit event
